title: Fluorescent Labeling and Imaging of IL-22 mRNA-Loaded Lipid Nanoparticles
author: Rabeya Jafrin Mow
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: 1,1'-Dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-Tetramethylindotricarbocyanine Iodide (DiR') (Thermo Scientific, Invitrogen TM , catalog number: D12731 ) Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) (Fisher Scientific, catalog number: BP231-
Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) (Corning, catalog number: 21-040-CV) Laboratory supplies 15 mL conical centrifuge tube (Thermo Scientific, Nunc TM 15 mL, catalog number:
Amicon ® Ultra 15 mL centrifugal filter (Millipore, Ultracel ® -100k, catalog number: UFC
1 mL syringe PP/PE without needle (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: Z683531-100A) Petri dish (CELLTREAT, catalog number: 229620)

steps.title: Prepare IL-22 LNP suspension
steps.instruction: Prepare 5 mL of IL-22 mRNA‑loaded lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) in a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube according to the previously published protocol.

steps.title: Make DiR′ stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 mg of DiR′ powder in 1 mL dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to obtain a 5 mg/mL DiR′/DMSO solution.

steps.title: Add DiR′ to LNPs
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the 5 mg/mL DiR′/DMSO solution to the 5 mL IL‑22/LNP suspension in the 15 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Incubate labeling mixture
steps.instruction: Cover the tube with aluminum foil and incubate at room temperature for 15 min while shaking at 100 rpm on an orbital shaker.

steps.title: Purify DiR′‑labeled LNPs
steps.instruction: Transfer the labeled LNP suspension into 15 mL centrifugal filters (each receiving 2.5 mL), centrifuge at 4,696×g for 10 min at 10 °C, discard the filtrate, add 1 mL PBS to each filter, resuspend by pipetting more than 100 times, then collect the suspension in a 5 mL Eppendorf tube.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 2.5 mL of the labeled suspension into each centrifugal filter.
Remove the filter from the centrifuge.
Add 1 mL PBS to each filter.
Resuspend the retained LNPs by repeated pipetting (>100 times).
Transfer the final suspension to a 5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Fast and group mice
steps.instruction: Fast healthy C57BL/6J mice for 4 h, then divide them into a control group and a treated group.

steps.title: Load syringe with labeled LNPs
steps.instruction: Fill a 1 mL syringe equipped with a curved feeding needle with the DiR′‑labeled IL‑22/LNP suspension and remove all air bubbles.

steps.title: Oral gavage of mice
steps.instruction: Manually restrain each mouse, insert the feeding needle into the mouth and esophagus, and administer 200 µL of DiR′‑labeled IL‑22/LNP suspension to the treated group; administer 200 µL of free (unlabeled) LNP suspension to the control group. If resistance is felt, retract and reposition the needle.

steps.title: Post‑gavage fasting
steps.instruction: Fast the mice for an additional 1 h after gavage.

steps.title: Harvest GI tract
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mice 24 h after gavage, dissect, and collect the gastrointestinal (GI) tract.

steps.title: Prepare IVIS instrument
steps.instruction: Turn on the IVIS Spectrum CT instrument 45 min before imaging, launch the Living Image software, click the initializing button, and wait until the temperature indicator turns green (CCD camera reaches –90 °C).

substeps.instruction: Turn on IVIS Spectrum CT 45 min prior to the test.
Start Living Image software and click the initializing button.
Wait until the temperature button turns green, indicating the CCD camera has reached –90 °C.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Place the harvested GI tract (both treated and control samples) in the imaging chamber, set the imaging mode to fluorescence with excitation at 745 nm and emission at 800 nm, acquire the images, and save them to the designated folder.

substeps.instruction: Place the GI tract specimens in the IVIS imaging chamber.
Select fluorescence mode; set excitation filter to 745 nm and emission filter to 800 nm.
Click Acquire in the acquisition control panel.
Save the acquired images to the appropriate path.
